# Training Method

## Initialisation from Feature Selection

First we must initialise the data from the previous file ` 02---Feature-Engineering-and-Selection` to create our analysis, so this is purely repeated:

```{r}
create_features_by_date <- function(data, k, day_levels = NULL) {

  data <- data |>
    arrange(Date)

  if (nrow(data) == 0) {
    return(data)
  }

  if (is.null(day_levels)) {
    day_levels <- sort(unique(
      as.character(data$DayOfWeek[!is.na(data$DayOfWeek)])
    ))
  }

  # Identify teams in each season
  season_teams <- lapply(
    split(data, as.character(data$SeasonStart)),
    function(x) {
      unique(c(
        as.character(x$HomeTeam),
        as.character(x$AwayTeam)
      ))
    }
  )

  # Initialise all team histories and standings
  teams <- unique(c(
    as.character(data$HomeTeam),
    as.character(data$AwayTeam)
  ))

  state <- initialise_state(teams)

  dates <- sort(unique(data$Date))

  output <- vector("list", length(dates))

  # Process matches by date
  for (d in seq_along(dates)) {

    current_date <- dates[d]

    today <- data |>
      filter(Date == current_date)

    season <- as.character(today$SeasonStart[1])

    # Handle season changes
    if (
      is.null(state$current_season) ||
      state$current_season != season
    ) {

      state <- start_season_fast(
        state,
        season,
        season_teams[[season]]
      )
    }

    # Calculate every fixture's features BEFORE updating results
    today_features <- create_today_features_fast(
      today = today,
      state = state,
      k = k,
      day_levels = day_levels
    )

    output[[d]] <- today_features

    # Only update histories using completed matches
    completed <- which(
      !is.na(today$HomeGoals) &
      !is.na(today$AwayGoals)
    )

    for (j in completed) {

      state <- update_state_fast(
        state,
        as.character(today$HomeTeam[j]),
        as.character(today$AwayTeam[j]),
        today$HomeGoals[j],
        today$AwayGoals[j]
      )
    }
  }

  bind_rows(output)
}

```



```{r}
get_recent_stats_fast <- function(history, k, venue = NULL) {

  if (is.null(venue)) {
    indices <- seq_along(history$GF)
  } else {
    indices <- which(history$Venue == venue)
  }

  indices <- tail(indices, k)

  if (length(indices) == 0) {
    return(list(
      GoalsScored = 0,
      GoalsConceded = 0,
      Points = 0,
      Wins = 0,
      Draws = 0,
      Losses = 0,
      Matches = 0
    ))
  }

  list(
    GoalsScored = mean(history$GF[indices]),
    GoalsConceded = mean(history$GA[indices]),
    Points = mean(history$Points[indices]),
    Wins = sum(history$Points[indices] == 3),
    Draws = sum(history$Points[indices] == 1),
    Losses = sum(history$Points[indices] == 0),
    Matches = length(indices)
  )
}

```



```{r}

initialise_state <- function(teams) {

  empty_history <- function() {
    list(
      GF = numeric(),
      GA = numeric(),
      Points = numeric(),
      Venue = character()
    )
  }

  list(
    history = setNames(
      lapply(teams, function(x) empty_history()),
      teams
    ),

    standings = matrix(
      0,
      nrow = length(teams),
      ncol = 3,
      dimnames = list(
        teams,
        c("Points", "GF", "GA")
      )
    ),

    current_season = NULL,
    current_teams = NULL,
    previous_positions = NULL,
    starting_positions = NULL
  )
}

```


```{r}
start_season_fast <- function(state, season, current_teams) {

  # Calculate previous season's final positions
  if (!is.null(state$current_season)) {

    previous_table <- data.frame(
      Team = state$current_teams,
      Points = state$standings[state$current_teams, "Points"],
      GF = state$standings[state$current_teams, "GF"],
      GA = state$standings[state$current_teams, "GA"]
    )

    previous_table$GD <-
      previous_table$GF - previous_table$GA

    previous_table <- previous_table[
      order(
        -previous_table$Points,
        -previous_table$GD,
        -previous_table$GF,
        previous_table$Team
      ),
    ]

    state$previous_positions <- setNames(
      seq_len(nrow(previous_table)),
      previous_table$Team
    )
  }

  state$current_season <- as.character(season)
  state$current_teams <- current_teams

  # Initialise previous-season positions
  state$starting_positions <- NULL

  if (!is.null(state$previous_positions)) {

    starting_positions <-
      state$previous_positions[current_teams]

    promoted <- is.na(starting_positions)

    # Give all promoted teams the same starting position
    if (any(promoted)) {

      starting_positions[promoted] <-
        max(state$previous_positions) + 1
    }

    state$starting_positions <- starting_positions
  }

  # Reset current-season standings
  state$standings[,] <- 0

  state
}

```


```{r}

update_state_fast <- function(state, home, away, hg, ag) {

  hp <- if (hg > ag) {
    3
  } else if (hg == ag) {
    1
  } else {
    0
  }

  ap <- if (ag > hg) {
    3
  } else if (ag == hg) {
    1
  } else {
    0
  }

  # Update home team's match history
  h <- state$history[[home]]

  h$GF <- c(h$GF, hg)
  h$GA <- c(h$GA, ag)
  h$Points <- c(h$Points, hp)
  h$Venue <- c(h$Venue, "Home")

  state$history[[home]] <- h

  # Update away team's match history
  a <- state$history[[away]]

  a$GF <- c(a$GF, ag)
  a$GA <- c(a$GA, hg)
  a$Points <- c(a$Points, ap)
  a$Venue <- c(a$Venue, "Away")

  state$history[[away]] <- a

  # Update league standings
  state$standings[home, "Points"] <-
    state$standings[home, "Points"] + hp

  state$standings[home, "GF"] <-
    state$standings[home, "GF"] + hg

  state$standings[home, "GA"] <-
    state$standings[home, "GA"] + ag

  state$standings[away, "Points"] <-
    state$standings[away, "Points"] + ap

  state$standings[away, "GF"] <-
    state$standings[away, "GF"] + ag

  state$standings[away, "GA"] <-
    state$standings[away, "GA"] + hg

  state
}

```


```{r}
get_current_table_fast <- function(state) {

  teams <- state$current_teams

  table_now <- data.frame(
    Team = teams,

    Points = unname(
      state$standings[teams, "Points"]
    ),

    GF = unname(
      state$standings[teams, "GF"]
    ),

    GA = unname(
      state$standings[teams, "GA"]
    )
  )

  table_now$GD <- table_now$GF - table_now$GA

  if (!is.null(state$starting_positions)) {

    table_now$PreviousPosition <-
      unname(state$starting_positions[table_now$Team])

  } else {

    table_now$PreviousPosition <- NA_real_
  }

  table_now <- table_now[
    order(
      -table_now$Points,
      -table_now$GD,
      -table_now$GF,
      table_now$PreviousPosition,
      na.last = TRUE
    ),
  ]

  table_now$Position <- seq_len(nrow(table_now))

  table_now
}

```


```{r}
create_today_features_fast <- function(
    today,
    state,
    k,
    day_levels
) {

  # Calculate the league table once for today's fixtures
  table_now <- get_current_table_fast(state)

  positions <- setNames(
    table_now$Position,
    table_now$Team
  )

  points <- setNames(
    table_now$Points,
    table_now$Team
  )

  goal_difference <- setNames(
    table_now$GD,
    table_now$Team
  )

  # Generate features for each fixture
  features <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(today)), function(i) {

    home <- as.character(today$HomeTeam[i])
    away <- as.character(today$AwayTeam[i])

    # Overall recent performance
    home_stats <- get_recent_stats_fast(
      state$history[[home]], k
    )

    away_stats <- get_recent_stats_fast(
      state$history[[away]], k
    )

    # Venue-specific recent performance
    home_venue_stats <- get_recent_stats_fast(
      state$history[[home]], k, venue = "Home"
    )

    away_venue_stats <- get_recent_stats_fast(
      state$history[[away]], k, venue = "Away"
    )

    data.frame(

      Date = today$Date[i],
      SeasonStart = today$SeasonStart[i],

      DayOfWeek = factor(
        as.character(today$DayOfWeek[i]),
        levels = day_levels
      ),

      HomeTeam = home,
      AwayTeam = away,

      # Overall recent performance
      Home_GS = home_stats$GoalsScored,
      Home_GC = home_stats$GoalsConceded,
      Home_Points = home_stats$Points,
      Home_Wins = home_stats$Wins,

      Away_GS = away_stats$GoalsScored,
      Away_GC = away_stats$GoalsConceded,
      Away_Points = away_stats$Points,
      Away_Wins = away_stats$Wins,

      # Venue-specific recent performance
      Home_Home_GS = home_venue_stats$GoalsScored,
      Home_Home_GC = home_venue_stats$GoalsConceded,

      Away_Away_GS = away_venue_stats$GoalsScored,
      Away_Away_GC = away_venue_stats$GoalsConceded,

      # League standings
      Home_Position = unname(positions[home]),
      Away_Position = unname(positions[away]),

      Home_Current_Points = unname(points[home]),
      Away_Current_Points = unname(points[away]),

      Home_GD = unname(goal_difference[home]),
      Away_GD = unname(goal_difference[away]),

      # Historical information
      Home_History = home_stats$Matches,
      Away_History = away_stats$Matches,

      # Response variables
      HomeGoals = today$HomeGoals[i],
      AwayGoals = today$AwayGoals[i]

    )
  })

  do.call(rbind, features)
}

## Training

As seen above and calculated in the feature engineering section, we have 4 different $k$ valued feature sets. However, we will use $k=5$ and `ntree=1000` as a baseline to calculate our home and away features as $k=5$ is not too large as to dilute recent information and lose any gain we might expect from recent data, but not too small that we don't have enough important history to make informed decisions with. We split training data given the features we chose in training into our home and away datasets, and we fit two random forests for home and away goals respectively. 


```{r}

X_home <- training_features |>
  select(all_of(home_features))

X_away <- training_features |>
  select(all_of(away_features))

set.seed(123)

rf_home <- randomForest(
  x = X_home,
  y = training_features$HomeGoals,
  ntree = 1000,
  mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(X_home))),
  importance = TRUE
)

rf_away <- randomForest(
  x = X_away,
  y = training_features$AwayGoals,
  ntree = 1000,
  mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(X_away))),
  importance = TRUE
)

```



# Testing

## Walk-forward Forecasting

Previously, I had decided to use a recursive forecast which means I would be using forecasted data to predict subsequent data, as would be the case if we had no future data to compare with such as on the 2026/27 data. However, our group decided unanimously to use actual data to improve our models as the season progresses. This is known as walk-forward forecasting, where after the model has predicted the goals of a match using historical data, it saves the predicted goals in the final results prediction but updates the model using what actually happened in the match in preparation for the next match between the teams. Therefore, even though our function is called `recursive_forecast`, it has been adapted to perform walk-forward forecasting. 

In our function, we first prepare the historical data and team composition to initialise the order of the matches within the season. We then create the history and league standings of each team before the season starts, preparing the current season features as an initialised state as previously used to make the features for training. We then create the storage of the future dates and fixtures, and a storage location for the predicted goals to live. We generate the sufficient features for each match and each team, and select the features we intend to use on each random forest respectively. We create a for loop that proceeds through each match and predicts the outcomes using the random forests, allocating the goals predicted to the storage location, rounding the goals to the nearest integer, and then updating each of the feature datasets with the outcome that actually happened. This is made using the `update_state_fast` function used in feature generation but we use the actual match outcome instead of the forecasted result. This removes the uncertainty posed by the recursive forecasting method as the model snaps back from straying too far from the real result like an elastic band by inserting the actual result to improve the models accuracy, instead of increasing variability by using uncertain predicted data in future prediction.  

```{r}
recursive_forecast_fast <- function(
    historical_data,
    future_fixtures,
    model_home,
    model_away,
    k,
    home_predictors,
    away_predictors,
    day_levels
) {

  # Clean and sort historical data
  historical_data <- historical_data |>
    filter(
      !is.na(HomeGoals),
      !is.na(AwayGoals)
    ) |>
    arrange(Date)

  future_fixtures <- future_fixtures |>
    arrange(Date)

  if (nrow(future_fixtures) == 0) {
    return(future_fixtures)
  }

  # Identify every team participating in each season
  season_rows <- bind_rows(
    historical_data |>
      select(SeasonStart, HomeTeam, AwayTeam),

    future_fixtures |>
      select(SeasonStart, HomeTeam, AwayTeam)
  )

  season_teams <- lapply(
    split(
      season_rows,
      as.character(season_rows$SeasonStart)
    ),
    function(x) {
      unique(c(
        as.character(x$HomeTeam),
        as.character(x$AwayTeam)
      ))
    }
  )

  # Initialise team histories and standings
  teams <- unique(c(
    as.character(historical_data$HomeTeam),
    as.character(historical_data$AwayTeam),
    as.character(future_fixtures$HomeTeam),
    as.character(future_fixtures$AwayTeam)
  ))

  state <- initialise_state(teams)

  # ------------------------------------------
  # 1. Process historical matches ONCE
  # ------------------------------------------

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(historical_data))) {

    match <- historical_data[i, ]

    season <- as.character(match$SeasonStart)

    # Check for season changes
    if (
      is.null(state$current_season) ||
      state$current_season != season
    ) {

      state <- start_season_fast(
        state,
        season,
        season_teams[[season]]
      )
    }

    # Update team histories and standings
    state <- update_state_fast(
      state,
      as.character(match$HomeTeam),
      as.character(match$AwayTeam),
      match$HomeGoals,
      match$AwayGoals
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------
  # 2. Forecast future matches chronologically
  # ------------------------------------------

  future_dates <- sort(unique(future_fixtures$Date))

  predictions <- vector(
    "list",
    length(future_dates)
  )

  for (d in seq_along(future_dates)) {

    current_date <- future_dates[d]

    # Extract today's fixtures
    today <- future_fixtures |>
      filter(Date == current_date)

    season <- as.character(today$SeasonStart[1])

    # Check whether a new season has started
    if (
      is.null(state$current_season) ||
      state$current_season != season
    ) {

      state <- start_season_fast(
        state,
        season,
        season_teams[[season]]
      )
    }

    # Generate features using the current state
    today_features <- create_today_features_fast(
      today = today,
      state = state,
      k = k,
      day_levels = day_levels
    )

    # Select predictors
    X_today_home <- today_features[
      ,
      home_predictors,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    X_today_away <- today_features[
      ,
      away_predictors,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    # Predict home and away goals
    home_predictions <- predict(
      model_home,
      newdata = X_today_home
    )

    away_predictions <- predict(
      model_away,
      newdata = X_today_away
    )

    # Convert predicted scores into non-negative integers
    today_predictions <- today

    today_predictions$PredictedHomeRaw <-
      as.numeric(home_predictions)

    today_predictions$PredictedAwayRaw <-
      as.numeric(away_predictions)

    today_predictions$PredictedHomeGoals <- pmax(
      0,
      round(home_predictions)
    )

    today_predictions$PredictedAwayGoals <- pmax(
      0,
      round(away_predictions)
    )

    # ------------------------------------------
    # 3. Update state AFTER all today's predictions
    # ------------------------------------------

    completed <- which(
  !is.na(today$HomeGoals) &
  !is.na(today$AwayGoals)
)

for (j in completed) {

  state <- update_state_fast(
    state,
    as.character(today$HomeTeam[j]),
    as.character(today$AwayTeam[j]),
    today$HomeGoals[j],
    today$AwayGoals[j]
  )
}

    # Save today's predictions
    predictions[[d]] <- today_predictions
  }

  # Combine all predicted matches once
  bind_rows(predictions)
}


```

Here is Anna's ranking table that we use to create the final ranking - see `Anna Del Pino/` for more info. 

```{r}
ranking <- function(matches, home_goals, away_goals) {
  #home rank
  home_points <-ifelse(home_goals > away_goals, 3, ifelse(home_goals == away_goals, 1, 0))
  home_ranking <- data.frame(Team = matches$HomeTeam, Points = home_points, GF = home_goals, GA = away_goals)
  #away rank
  away_points <- ifelse(away_goals > home_goals,3, ifelse(away_goals == home_goals, 1, 0))
  away_ranking <- data.frame(Team = matches$AwayTeam, Points = away_points, GF = away_goals, GA = home_goals)

  all_team_matches <- rbind(home_ranking, away_ranking)

  final_ranking <- aggregate(cbind(Points, GF, GA) ~ Team, data = all_team_matches, sum) #cbind(Points, GF, GA) combines those three columns as the response and ~ Team says to group the rows by Team. sum is the function applied to each column within each team’s group

  final_ranking$GD <- final_ranking$GF - final_ranking$GA #create new goal difference column for each team 
  
  #ordering
  final_ranking <- final_ranking[order(-final_ranking$Points, -final_ranking$GD), ] #order() uses GD to break ties in Points, so teams with the same points are ordered by highest goal difference first
  final_ranking$Position <- seq_len(nrow(final_ranking)) #adding a column that tells us the position

  final_ranking <- final_ranking[c("Position", "Team", "Points", "GD")]
  rownames(final_ranking) <- NULL

  final_ranking
}

```



## Testing using Training Features

Here, we partition our data into our historical and future data to prevent any leakage, and run our walk-forward algorithm which updates after each successive match. We input our features, both the home and away models, and we are provided with our predicted end of season table ranking. Due to the random nature of the random forest, some rankings may differ each time but overall the structure should be similar. 

```{r}
historical_data <- combined_data |>
  filter(SeasonStart >= 2014,
         SeasonStart <= 2024)

future_fixtures <- combined_data |>
  filter(SeasonStart == 2025)

predictions_2025_fast <- recursive_forecast_fast(

    historical_data = historical_data,
    future_fixtures = future_fixtures,

    model_home = rf_home,
    model_away = rf_away,

    k = 5,

    home_predictors = home_features,
    away_predictors = away_features,

    day_levels = levels(training_features$DayOfWeek)
  )


final_table_fast <- ranking(
  matches = predictions_2025_fast,
  home_goals = predictions_2025_fast$PredictedHomeGoals,
  away_goals = predictions_2025_fast$PredictedAwayGoals
)

final_table_fast

```
